problem: Prior vision-language navigation work handles only subsets of turn-based dialog navigation (mostly navigation from given instructions), and speaker-follower data augmentation fails when agents must also ask questions and give answers. No prior agent generates navigator questions and guide answers end-to-end on CVDN.
motivation: Efficient communication requires modeling the conversational partner (theory of mind) and the effect of a dialog act on future navigation. The paper argues that the best question is the one that elicits the answer that leads to the most goal progress, so reward from navigation should flow back into the language models.
key_idea: A recursive mental model (RMM) agent spawns instances of itself (navigator, questioner, guide) to roll out N sampled dialogs/trajectories and propagates goal-progress reward back through all three models via RL.
insight: Speaker-follower data augmentation collapses the language (only 22 lexical types), whereas RMM keeps over 500 types (humans use ~900), so the RL signal through recursive rollouts is what keeps the language useful and diverse. Human evaluation shows RMM's language is rated about as grammatical and fluent as the baseline, so it has not drifted into 'neuralese'. Ablations show that in seen houses the target-only model does best, suggesting search rather than dialog use, while RMM's gains appear in unseen houses.
method: Seq2Seq backbone: LSTM encoder over dialog history, LSTM action decoder with attention over language and ResNet image features. Speaker models (questioner Q, guide/oracle O) are bi-LSTM image encoders with attention-based word decoders.
Pretraining: navigator, questioner and guide are first trained on CVDN human dialogs (20k iterations) before self-play fine-tuning.
Recursive rollouts: each model samples N trajectories/generations (one argmax, the rest sampled), which are recursively expanded into dialogs, with a cap on total recursive calls.

RL training: navigator uses A2C with goal-progress reward plus cross-entropy on the shortest path. Speaker models are updated with generation cross-entropy plus the navigator loss from the branch with max goal progress.
Inference: because the remaining distance to the goal is unavailable at test time, the agent rolls out five navigation actions per sampled QA pair and keeps the highest-probability trajectory.

Dialog gameplay: the questioner is invoked every 4 navigation steps (a fixed heuristic, not learned), with up to 80 actions and 20 QA exchanges. A single generator handles both roles, conditioned by <NAV>/<ORA> tags.
Data augmentation baseline: the best of 3 sampled rollouts is paired with a generated instruction and added to training with weight lambda=0.1.

setting.backbone: LSTM encoder-decoder Seq2Seq navigator, questioner and guide with ResNet features (trained from scratch on CVDN, then RL)
setting.training_data: CVDN human-human dialogs (pretraining 20k iterations), then 5k iterations of self-play; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric panoramic RGB views in Matterport3D encoded by ResNet penultimate layer (512-d); target object name; dialog history
setting.action_space: low-level: forward, left, right, look up, look down, stop (max 80 actions)
setting.privileged: During training and for the guide model: the next 5 shortest-path steps as images and exact goal-progress reward. At test time the guide still sees the shortest-path views; the navigator uses only model confidence.

numbers.extra: Agent-agent dialog: guide gets oracle shortest-path views

numbers_note: Goal Progress in meters is stored under key GP. Table also has N=1 variants, QA-only context columns, and baselines (Seq2Seq val-seen full-history GP 15.0, val-unseen 4.6). Shortest path upper bound is 32.8 (seen) and 29.3 (unseen).
results: On val-unseen CVDN, RMM N=3 reaches 5.6 m goal progress with full dialog history versus 4.6 (Seq2Seq) and 4.4 (Seq2Seq+DA), and gets the best BLEU (2.9 vs 0.5/1.1). In seen houses it slightly underperforms the baseline (14.0 vs 15.0), which the authors attribute to environment bias. Goal progress remains far below the human and shortest-path levels (29.3 m unseen).
limitations: Agent-agent only, with the guide modeled as a copy of the agent and given oracle shortest-path views; no human-in-the-loop evaluation
Fixed question-asking schedule (every 4 steps) and fixed branching factor; the agent doesn't decide when to ask
Small absolute gains and weaker than baseline in seen houses; agents struggle to know when to stop, and the inference heuristic is confidence-based
